Herbert P. Gray, chairman and chief executive officer, commented, "The second quarter was the strongest recorded by Suburban Ostomy in its 18 years of operation. We are seeing steady internal sales and gross profit growth from our current base of business. In addition, we continue to evaluate acquisition opportunities and remain convinced that industry trends support a consolidating marketplace."

For the second quarter, the number of customer orders filled increased 30 percent to approximately 128,300 compared with 98,900 in the second quarter of last year. The average order size rose 6 percent to $182 from $171, primarily as a result of the mix of sales between Suburban Ostomy and acquired businesses. Of the $6.3 million increase in net sales, about 10 percent was attributable to same store growth while the remainder was due to the acquisitions.

Donald H. Benovitz, president and chief executive officer, said, "Our 'same store' business continued to grow in the second quarter. Suburban Ostomy remains the choice for home medical equipment suppliers and independent pharmacies and we are steadily increasing our penetration of the national home health care chain and managed care segments. Although it can take an extended period of time to develop initial relationships with these new types of customers, we have signed two significant contracts in recent months."

"First, we recently added an agreement with a health care industry uniform supplier amounting to approximately $1.5 million in annual revenue. In addition, after the end of the quarter we signed an agreement with the Med Group, one of the home health care industry's oldest networks supporting their 110 home care provider members. These types of agreements illustrate the benefit of our comprehensive product offering, with over 6,000 SKUs focused on home health care needs, and superior customer service and technical support with highly efficient order fulfillment and timely delivery. In addition, we offer programs specifically targeted to the needs of national organizations, including a stockless inventory program and specialized patient utilization reporting," Benovitz added.

Benovitz said that Suburban's experience has been that the company's market leadership position allows it to have higher gross margins than others in the industry. As the company makes acquisitions, its goal is to carefully and slowly increase the gross margins of acquired businesses without significantly impacting sales and customer retention. "Most of the customers of the two companies we acquired in 1996 have been enthusiastic about improved delivery times, higher order fulfillment rates, the broad range of product offerings and other actions that we have implemented while accepting modest price increases. Across the board we are retaining the higher margin business, although overall retention rates are somewhat below our original expectations. We continue to implement outbound telemarketing and direct mail campaigns to reach all of the customers of the acquired businesses."
The company noted that it is continuing to pursue judicial remedies, as stated last quarter, against a former St. Louis Ostomy employee to determine if new competition in that market was legitimate.
Benefits of Larger Base of Business Illustrated in Results

For the second quarter, gross profit increased 41 percent to $5.5 million from $3.9 million. The gross margin for the second quarter was 23.9 percent, higher than the 23.5 percent gross margin reported for the same quarter last year and the first quarter of this year. Operating expenses were $2.9 million vs. $2.0 million a year ago. Depreciation and amortization expense was $219,000 compared with $92,000 due to the amortization of goodwill associated with previous acquisitions.

Benovitz commented, "Suburban Ostomy has long commanded solid margins within the home health care distribution industry because of the added value we provide our customers. This quarter's results again confirmed our position within the industry, with earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization rising to a record $2.6 million, or 11.3 percent of revenue. In addition, with our larger base of business, we are gaining additional support and recognition from vendors, who value what we bring to the market. Our recent results also reflect our ability to partner with vendors that have chosen to turn over their smaller volume direct business to the wholesale market."
Strong Financial Position Sets Stage for Acquisitions

Total assets at March 1, 1997 were $38.1 million compared with $33.1 million at year-end 1996, with cash and equivalents at $7.2 million compared with $2.0 million. Shareholders' equity at the end of the second quarter was $30.2 million compared with a deficit of $18.0 million at year- end. In addition, as a result of the recent public offering, virtually all long-term debt has been eliminated.

Turning to the company's acquisition strategy, Benovitz commented, "The home health care distribution industry is highly fragmented, with a number of local and regional wholesalers. Health care payors have demonstrated a preference for home health care providers that serve as a cost-effective, one- stop shop source for a comprehensive range of products. We believe that Suburban Ostomy can take advantage of these market conditions to make additional acquisitions that add to our customer base and/or expand our product offering and sales channels and we are actively pursuing opportunities," Benovitz concluded.

Suburban Ostomy Supply Co., Inc., which completed its initial public offering in October 1996, is a direct marketing wholesaler of medical supplies and related products to the home health care industry. The company sells products to over 22,000 customers, including: home medical equipment suppliers and pharmacies; national home health care chains; and, managed care organizations. Through its direct sales and marketing programs, the company markets a comprehensive selection of more than 6,000 stock keeping units, primarily products for ostomy, incontinence, diabetic and wound care. The company's common stock is being traded on the Nasdaq National Market System under the symbol SOSC.

This release contains forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties inherent in the company's business. The company's actual results could differ materially from those anticipated in those forward- looking statements as a result of certain factors, including those set forth in documents filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission including the prospectus dated October 9, 1996, related to the company's recently completed initial public offering, and the recently filed 10K.
